title: Dumbbell Bench Press
summary: Flat bench press with dumbbells: chest 1, front delts 0.5, triceps 0.4. More stretch and freer arm path than a barbell, less load.

muscles.why: The pecs bring the upper arm across the body. Dumbbells can go lower than a bar, so the chest stretches more at the bottom.
The front delts help bring the arm forward (0.5).
The triceps finish the press; with no bar to push apart they rate lower than on a barbell (0.4 vs 0.5).

setup.text: Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs and kick them up as you lie back.
Shoulder blades back and down, feet planted.
Start with the dumbbells over your chest, arms straight.

form_cues.cue: Lower until the dumbbells are level with your chest
form_cues.why: Lowering to the sides of the chest is where the press lines up with the pec.
Wrists over elbows keeps the push straight up.
Stopping just short of touching keeps tension on.
The hands come together a little at the top, following the chest's line.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower until the elbows are a little below the bench
bias_tweaks.effect: Uses the deeper stretch dumbbells allow.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Go as deep as is comfortable for your shoulders.

bias_tweaks.effect: Many lifters find the shoulders more comfortable.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Cutting the range short at the bottom to move heavier dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about 45-70 degrees from the torso at the bottom.

mistakes.text: Cutting the bottom short to use heavier dumbbells.
mistakes.fix: Use the full range; it is the main reason to pick dumbbells.

mistakes.text: Dropping the dumbbells from the top.
mistakes.fix: Bring them to the chest and sit up, or lower them to the sides with control.

misconceptions.myth: You need to bench with a barbell to build the chest.
misconceptions.reality: Free weights and machines gave similar growth; press variations swap well.
Low-load bench (40% 1RM) and push-ups grew the pecs and triceps similarly when taken hard.

lower_risk.text: The app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the first working load is at least 18 kg (40 lb) per hand and the main muscle is not already warm from an earlier lift. Otherwise start with a slightly lighter first set.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 8-12 rep range. End the set before the dumbbells start to drift out of line.
Getting the dumbbells into place and out is part of the lift: kick them up from the thighs, and at the end bring them to the chest and sit up.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Same press with a bar: more load, less stretch.
Machine path, easy to push close to failure.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: No equipment; grew the pecs similarly to light bench press when taken hard.

notes: Dumbbell vs barbell bench has not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
